title: Jockeys, Owners & Trainers
subtitle: Licences, trainer assignments and jockey contracts
summary: Racing Participants manages who is allowed to take part in racing: jockey, trainer, owner and official licences with validity and status, which trainer has each horse, and jockey retainer contracts. Race Operations checks it live for every entry and every race official.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: A licence is a dated permission issued by an authority. Issuing or renewing one charges the licence fee for its type (LICENCE_JOCKEY, LICENCE_TRAINER ...) as an accounting event, which AR turns into an invoice to the holder.

Trainer assignments are effective-dated like ownership: assigning a new trainer ends the previous assignment the day before. When a steward enters a horse and leaves the trainer blank, Race Operations asks this service who trains the horse on race day.
A nightly job expires licences whose end date has passed; its changes appear in the audit trail as system:licence-expiry.

sections.title: Racing Participants database architecture · Visual ERD
sections.intro: The physical MySQL model contains three domain tables and five declared foreign keys. Those five relationships connect to three shared reference tables in enterprise_core and horse_registry.

sections.title: What the five database relationships actually mean
rows: A licence belongs to an existing person or organisation recorded in the shared party master.
Trainer assignments can refer only to horses that exist in Horse Registry.
The trainer is an existing shared party, not a duplicate person record.
The jockey under contract is an identified party, connected to other business roles.
The contractual party on the club side is a registered legal entity.

sections.title: A race-day story: who may ride, train, and officiate?
paragraphs: 1. A person enters the party register. Imagine jockey Hannah Whitfield already exists as a party in Enterprise Core. A licence is not another person record; it is a permission granted to that person for a specified role and period.

2. A licence has two dimensions. participant_license stores the category (JOCKEY, TRAINER, OWNER or OFFICIAL), the issuing authority, licence number, valid-from/valid-to dates, and status. A status of ACTIVE alone does not prove the licence remains valid on race day.

3. Training a horse is a separate assignment. horse_trainer_assignment links an existing horse to a trainer party for an effective date range. This is distinct from the trainer’s licence and allows historical inquiries.

4. Employment or retainer arrangements are different again. jockey_contract captures the jockey, the Turf Club legal entity, start/end dates, base fee and currency. A contract is not itself proof of a valid licence.

5. Race Operations must ask the right question. On the date of a race it should confirm an appropriate active, in-date licence, the applicable trainer assignment, and any other racing rules before accepting a participant. Whether the live application enforces all these checks should be demonstrated against its actual endpoints.

sections.title: Video-ready walkthrough: from licence to racing decision
items: Hook (30 seconds): “A jockey’s licence expires on Friday. Can she ride on Saturday? Why is a database foreign key not enough to decide?”
Shared master data (1 minute): Show enterprise_core.party, then reveal why the participant module stores role-specific records rather than copies of people.
Explain the ERD (2 minutes): Follow the five arrows, distinguish references from domain tables, and explain licence, trainer assignment and jockey contract.
Live demo (3 minutes): Use the existing lesson’s renew / reject / validate sequence, checking the actual UI behavior.
Business rules (1 minute): Compare SQL constraints to date-effective and status-sensitive eligibility.
Cross-module consequence (1 minute): Show how Race Operations consults participant eligibility. Discuss fee posting only in the context of observed application behavior.
Closing question: “Would your cloud architecture catch an expired licence before allowing a race entry—or only after a customer complaint?”

sections.title: Design decisions
items: Licences are separate rows per type, so one person can be both trainer and jockey with independent lifecycles.
Overlap rules (one active licence per type, one trainer per horse at a time, one contract per jockey and entity) are database guards.
